title: The Priestly Garments
intro: The high priest Aaron's clothing was not ordinary attire - they were sacred garments filled with symbolism. Each part represented aspects of God's character and the priest's role as mediator between God and the people.

items.title: Ephod
items.text: A robe made of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen. It was skillfully woven with two onyx stones on the shoulders bearing the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.

items.title: Breastpiece (Breastplate)
items.text: A square piece with twelve precious stones - one for each tribe. The Urim and Thummim were also kept here to seek God's will.

items.title: Robe
items.text: A solid blue robe with pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn along the hem, interspersed with gold bells. The bells were to be heard when the priest entered and exited the holy place.

items.title: Tunic and Sash
items.text: A patterned tunic of fine linen and a skillfully woven sash.

items.title: Turban with Gold Plate
items.text: A turban of fine linen with a plate of pure gold on the front inscribed: "Holy to the Lord".

items.title: Garments for the Other Priests
items.text: Aaron's sons were to wear tunics, sashes, and head coverings - for glory and beauty.

footer.title: Christ as High Priest
footer.content: The book of Hebrews shows that Jesus is our high priest - not with earthly garments, but with His own perfection. He carries us on His heart and enters the heavenly holy place for us.
